s: Family lines from Adam through Abraham, Isaac and Esau.
The sons of Israel and the family of Judah.
The descendants of David and the royal line.
More families of Judah, including Jabez's prayer, and of Simeon.
The tribes east of the Jordan: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh.
The family of Levi, the temple singers, and the towns of the Levites.
The families of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher.
The family of Benjamin, down to Saul.
Those who returned to live in Jerusalem after the exile, and the duties of the Levites. Saul's family line.
Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa because Saul was unfaithful to the Lord.
David is anointed king over all Israel and takes Jerusalem. His mighty men.
The warriors from every tribe who joined David.
David tries to bring the ark to Jerusalem, and Uzza dies for touching it.
David's household grows and he defeats the Philistines.
David prepares a place, and the Levites carry the ark into Jerusalem with music and joy.
The ark is placed in its tent. David appoints singers and gives a psalm of thanks.
God promises David an everlasting house and kingdom. David prays in gratitude.
David's victories and his officials.
War with the Ammonites and Syrians.
Rabbah is captured. More battles with the Philistine giants.
David's census brings a plague. He buys Ornan's threshing floor, the future site of the temple.
David gathers materials for the temple and charges Solomon to build it.
David makes Solomon king and organizes the Levites.
The priests are divided into twenty-four groups for temple service.
The temple musicians and their groups.
The gatekeepers, treasurers and other officials.
The army divisions and leaders of the tribes.
David gives Solomon the plans for the temple and urges him to be strong.
The leaders give generously for the temple. David blesses God, Solomon is anointed, and David dies.
